Fact.Name: Flow knockout: Form 8949 adjustment code Q (section 1202 exclusion)
Fact.Description: True when any Form 8949 row's code field (column (f)) contains the code letter Q, upper or lower case. Form 8949 instr. (2025) p. 8, code Q: "You sold or exchanged QSB stock and can exclude part of the gain" (the section 1202 exclusion, entered as a negative amount in column (g)). Under IRC §1(h)(4)(A)(ii) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1) 28-percent rate gain includes "section 1202 gain", which §1(h)(7) defines as "the excess of (A) the gain which would be excluded from gross income under section 1202 but for the percentage limitation in section 1202(a), over (B) the gain excluded from gross income under section 1202". That amount goes on Schedule D line 18 (Schedule D instr. (2025), Line 18, 28% Rate Gain Worksheet), and a nonzero line 18 means line 20 is No and the tax is figured on the Schedule D Tax Worksheet, which this tool does not compute (scheduleD3.xml uses the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet only). The row does not say which section 1202(a) percentage applies, so any code Q stops the return. A blank code field is complete and not Q; no rows is false.

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 5 amount from this sale
Fact.Description: #78: column (h). #80 part-year: only sales in the PA residency period; PA-40 IN (2025) p. 43, a nonresident does not pay PA tax on "any gain you realize on the sale, exchange, or disposition of intangible personal property, such as stocks and bonds."

Fact.Name: PA Schedule SP line 6: gain or loss from this sale while living outside PA
Fact.Description: #107: PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, line 6: "6. Non-PA income. Part-year residents and nonresidents must complete this line. Enter the total of all income, not already reported on this schedule, that you (and your spouse, if applicable) earned, received or realized while residing outside Pennsylvania." A part-year resident's sale dated outside the PA residency period (not /form8949Transactions/*/paSoldWhilePaResident) is not on PA-40 line 5, so its column (h) amount goes to line 6. Full-year residents and PA-period sales: $0.

Fact.Name: Gain or loss
Fact.Description: Form 8949 column (h): rounded column (d) − rounded column (e) ± rounded column (g) (Form 8949 instr. (2025) p.11, "Column (h)—Gain (or Loss)" Examples 1–3).

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (d) rounded to whole dollars
Fact.Description: Form 8949 column (d) Proceeds (sales price), ../proceeds rounded once to whole dollars (50 cents and up round up). Columns (d), (e) and (g) are rounded per row and column (h) is figured from the rounded amounts, so (d) - (e) + (g) = (h) on every row and on every line 2 total and Schedule D line. Each row is an amount entered on Form 8949; Form 1040 instr. (2025), "Rounding Off to Whole Dollars": "If you do round to whole dollars, you must round all amounts. To round, drop amounts under 50 cents and increase amounts from 50 to 99 cents to the next dollar." Gain or loss is (d) - (e) under IRC 1001(a).

Columns (d), (e) and (g) are rounded per row and column (h) is figured from the rounded amounts, so (d) - (e) + (g) = (h) on every row and on every line 2 total and Schedule D line. Each row is an amount entered on Form 8949; Form 1040 instr. (2025), "Rounding Off to Whole Dollars": "If you do round to whole dollars, you must round all amounts.
